system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
Seller “FINAL”/market-context statements are negotiation positions only, not binding on Buyer.

| Issue | Seller position | Buyer should want | Recommendation / one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at **20%** of price ($4.8m). | Higher general cap, with separate uncapped/price-capped regimes for protected categories. | **Reject as sole cap; seek at least 30% for general warranties.** A $4.8m cap may be inadequate for a $24m acquisition with concentrated customer and compliance risk. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | $25k de minimis; $250k aggregate deductible basket. | Lower de minimis and a lower, preferably tipping, basket. | **Counter at $10k de minimis and $100k tipping basket.** The proposed thresholds exclude multiple smaller but related losses and make recovery unnecessarily difficult. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | General claims must be notified within 18 months. | At least 24 months for general warranties, with longer separate periods for tax, IP, title and specific risks. | **Seek 24 months for general warranties.** Eighteen months may expire before annual-cycle, customer-contract and regulatory issues become identifiable. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same 20% cap and time limit as general warranties. | Title/capacity at least capped at 100% of price, with a longer period; no basket. | **Reject; create a separate fundamental-warranties regime.** Buyer must have full recourse if Seller did not own or could not transfer all shares. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all claims. | Express carve-out for fraud, fraudulent concealment and wilful misconduct. | **Insert an express fraud carve-out from every limitation and exclusive-remedy provision.** Seller must not be able to contractually shelter deliberate dishonesty. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of all indexed data-room material and public registers. | Only matters **fairly and specifically disclosed** against identified warranties, with sufficient detail to identify nature and scope. | **Reject blanket data-room/public-record disclosure.** A data dump does not give Buyer meaningful notice of a risk or its implications. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer/advisers, including matters discoverable in the data room or public records. | Actual knowledge only of specified Buyer deal-team members; no constructive knowledge or adviser-imputation standard. | **Delete “discoverable” and adviser-knowledge wording.** Buyer should not lose warranty protection merely because a fact could theoretically have been found. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Seller will use reasonable endeavours; consent treated as addressed upon written counterparty consent. No final consent or evidence of conditions being satisfied. | Completion condition requiring consent in form satisfactory to Buyer and satisfaction/waiver of all linked conditions, with no adverse amendment or termination right. | **Make Bluefen consent and all conditions precedent to Completion, or require robust holdback/indemnity and termination right.** Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | Approx. $3.2m facility to be addressed by release provided after Completion. | Repayment at or before Completion and contemporaneous irrevocable release of all security/guarantees. | **Require pay-off and releases as a Completion deliverable, funded through the funds flow.** Buyer cannot acquire a purportedly debt-free company with outstanding secured debt. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | $420k conditional completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; no treatment of payroll tax, super or on-costs. | Treat all bonuses and associated employment on-costs as Seller-funded/debt-like amounts, or require a dollar-for-dollar price reduction/escrow and indemnity. | **Include the full liability and on-costs in the Completion adjustment or Seller payment obligation.** These are transaction-triggered liabilities which Buyer should not inherit without price protection. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment only; $180k remains open and IP transfer depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. | Confirmed assignment/title to all project materials, payment resolution, and a broad specific indemnity for all IP ownership/use losses. | **Require payment and written IP assignment/confirmation before Completion, backed by a specific uncapped or price-capped indemnity.** The target may otherwise lack ownership of material developed IP. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary incident; no confirmed unauthorised access, scope or notification obligation; Seller says not expected to be material. | Full investigation and remediation, ongoing disclosure covenant, Buyer control/approval of notifications, and specific indemnity/holdback for incident costs and liabilities. | **Do not accept “preliminary” as resolution; require a completion condition or ring-fenced indemnity/escrow.** Privacy exposure can crystallise after Completion through notification, regulatory action and remediation costs. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals total $330k and are said to be ordinary-course operating costs. | Full contracts and timing, confirmation of binding/termination status, and protection against undisclosed pre-Completion commitments. | **Require specific disclosure and either price adjustment or a covenant/indemnity for commitments outside agreed ordinary course.** “Ordinary course” does not establish that the obligations are avoidable or properly reflected in price. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | Seller seeks all limitations for all claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | Separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, IP, restrictive covenants and specific indemnities. | **Reject a universal limitations clause.** Distinct risk categories require distinct caps, baskets, time periods and remedy treatment. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register showing Seller holds 100%; no Buyer verification statement. | Unqualified title, capacity and no-encumbrance warranties; current register, ASIC/company searches, original certificates (if any), executed transfer and releases. | **Require independent title verification and Completion title deliverables.** A register extract alone does not establish absence of competing interests, options or security interests. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says tax and IP warranties are under the general regime. | Separate tax deed/indemnity for all pre-Completion tax and distinct IP title/infringement warranties, with longer survival and higher or full-price caps. | **Reject treatment solely under the general regime.** Pre-Completion tax and IP-chain defects can be material, latent and disproportionately costly. |
=== END ADVICE ===
